payload.summary: Registered falsifiable prediction CONFIRMED on the next cycle. Reader is the rounding model. New finding: the agent held the correct nominal tick and still keyed off wall clock, because neither the shared SKILL nor the agent flow mentions the scheduled_utc token it already receives. Prior claim of structural unhittability WITHDRAWN and corrected to ~68%.
payload.prediction_result:
PREDICTION CONFIRMED, and it discriminated between the two candidate reader models.

Registered before the agent returned (commit d424f9a6c, signal cowork-team-20260825T073518Z.json):
"Predicted: alert-commander MISSES the tick-snapshot and falls through to direct get_cycle_bootstrap.
A reader applying the SKILL's documented rounding computes 07:35; a raw-wall-clock reader computes
~07:36. Neither equals 07:34. Falsifier: a reported tick-snapshot HIT this cycle refutes the
mechanism and re-opens the analysis."

Observed (alert-commander notebook c252, committed f13212cf2, verbatim):
"no fresh tick-snapshot (no cycle-snapshot-07:35.json) -> direct get_cycle_bootstrap"

MISS as predicted. The lookup key was 07:35 -- the ROUNDING model, not the raw one. The file on disk
was cycle-snapshot-07:34.json (dispatcher wrote it 07:34:24). Falsifier did not occur.
payload.new_finding:
NEW AND SHARPER THAN THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS: the reader HAD the correct nominal tick and did not use it.

c252's own notebook header reads "2026-08-25T07:37:30Z (slot=alert-commander-market, tick=07:30)".
07:30 is the nominal tick -- it arrived as the scheduled_utc=<ISO> prompt token that
spawn-fanout.md Step 5.2 appends to every ENTRY_PROMPT, and the agent demonstrably read it, because
it echoed it into its own header. It then computed the snapshot key from its own wall clock anyway
(07:37:30 -> rounded 07:35) instead of from the nominal tick it was holding.

Root cause of THAT, measured not inferred -- two greps, both zero hits:
  grep -n "scheduled_utc|SCHEDULED|nominal" .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md  -> 0
  grep -rn "scheduled_utc" docs/agents/alert-commander/                              -> 0
The token arrives but no documented step in the reader's own flow or in the shared SKILL tells it
what to do with it. Whether a given cycle keys off the nominal tick is therefore LLM discretion, not
a rule -- which is why the three cycles today are mutually inconsistent:
  c250 ran 07:08:22Z, header tick=07:05, looked for 07:05  (neither nominal nor rounded-from-07:08)
  c251 ran 07:24:44Z, header tick=07:22, looked for 07:22  (raw, UNrounded)
  c252 ran 07:37:30Z, header tick=07:30, looked for 07:35  (rounded)
Three cycles of one agent, three different derivations. Do not model the reader as having one rule.
payload.self_correction:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN PRIOR CLAIM -- signal f1f413ca3 said the cache is "structurally unhittable".
That is too strong and I am withdrawing it.

It hits whenever the dispatcher's raw wall clock happens to land ON a 5-minute boundary and the
agent's rounded clock lands on the same one. Re-measured this tick across every snapshot file on
disk: 41 files, 13 on a 5-minute boundary (31.7%), 28 off (68.3%).

c250 is exactly that coincidence and it was a genuine HIT -- notebook verbatim:
"CYCLE_SNAPSHOT hit (cycle-snapshot-07:05.json, ~1min fresh)". Dispatcher wrote 07:05 at 07:05:09;
on-boundary; agent rounded to the same key.

Today's observed hit rate is 1 of 3 cycles (33%) against an on-boundary share of 31.7%. The cache
hit rate IS the on-boundary rate. That correspondence is the strongest corroboration of the
mechanism so far -- stronger than the miss itself, because it predicts the hits too, not just the
failures. But it means the defect costs ~68% of lookups, not 100%.
payload.recommended_fix:
FIX IS NOW CHEAPER AND MORE PRECISE THAN ORIGINALLY ROUTED. One value already flows end-to-end:
spawn-fanout.md Step 5.2's scheduled_utc=<ISO> token, derived ONCE by
cowork-catchup-predicate.mostRecentCronFireBefore (match-slots.md is explicit that this is one
derivation, not two, precisely to avoid peer-straddle bugs). It is already proven to arrive and be
read -- c252's header, and chef's marker key published:chef-intraday:2026-08-25:14 which was dated
from it rather than from date -u.

Delete BOTH wall clocks; have both sides derive from that single token:
 (W) tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7 -- FILE_TICK=$(date -u +%H:%M) sets both the FILENAME and the in-file
     .tick field. A rename-only fix is insufficient; the raw value is written into the document too.
 (R) .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md Step -1 -- key on the scheduled_utc token; fall back to
     rounded wall clock only when the token is absent (guaranteed-slot firer path, which omits it).

Same class as the already-shipped FIX-CHEF-MARKER-KEY-ANCHOR-3.

Third item, unchanged and still required: the SKILL carries a stale note saying "The snapshot writer
(cowork-team dispatcher) is a future task. Until it lands, Step -1 will always miss and fall through
to Step 0 -- zero behavior regression." The writer HAS landed. That sentence tells all 8 consuming
agents a miss is expected, which is why none of them ever escalated it. It must be deleted as part
of the same change, not filed separately.

BLAST RADIUS unchanged: 8 agents consume this SKILL (alert-commander, market-watcher, news-scout,
digest-predict, bctc-analyst, qa-responder, unified-agent, fb-market-poster-adjacent).
